qc.label_under_test: On the word right after me or us that opens a description of me or us (often 'as', 'a', 'for', 'my' or 'our') when a characterisation bounces back: an earlier clause has me or us characterising another person or group (seeing, regarding, calling or thinking them something, or praising, admiring, criticising, thanking, rewarding or punishing them for something), and the next clause has that person or group characterise me or us in the same way. Weaker: the same two-way swap between third-person pronouns. Silent: a returned attitude with no description of me or us after the pronoun (they trusted us, he feared me); a one-way characterisation of me or us with no earlier clause; me or us characterised first and then answering back; an ordinary returned action (visiting, lending, paying, hugging back); a characterisation aimed at a thing rather than a person.

neighbours.label: On the word right after me or us that opens a description of me or us (often 'as', 'a', 'for', 'my' or 'our') when a characterisation bounces back: an earlier clause has me or us characterising another person or group (seeing, regarding, calling or thinking them something, or praising, admiring, criticising, thanking, rewarding or punishing them for something), and the next clause has that person or group characterise me or us in the same way. Weaker: the same two-way swap between third-person pronouns. Silent: a returned attitude with no description of me or us after the pronoun (they trusted us, he feared me); a one-way characterisation of me or us with no earlier clause; me or us characterised first and then answering back; an ordinary returned action (visiting, lending, paying, hugging back); a characterisation aimed at a thing rather than a person.
fire: We had always seen the neighbours as rivals, and it turned out they saw us as rivals too.
I regarded him as a mentor, and he came to regard me as a friend.
We thanked the volunteers for their patience, and they thanked us for our hospitality.
I called her a genius, and she laughed and called me a flatterer.
We admired the visiting team for their discipline, and they admired us for our spirit.
I thought of my cousin as a bit of a show-off, and apparently he thought of me as a snob.
We criticised the council for its delays, and the council criticised us for our impatience.
When I praised the students for their effort, they praised me for my clear lectures.
quiet: We had always seen the neighbours as rivals, and it turned out they trusted us anyway.
I regarded him as a mentor, and he respected me deeply.
We thanked the volunteers for their patience, and they visited us again the next summer.
I called her a genius, and she hugged me back.
The visiting team admired us for our spirit after the match.
My cousin thought of me as a snob, and I told him he was a show-off.
We criticised the council for its delays, and the council paid us back the fees.
When I praised the students for their effort, they smiled at me and kept working.
